summary: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships are one-year Master's scholarships for the 2027/28 UK intake, run by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC) and funded by the UK government with participating UK universities. They are for high-quality postgraduate students from 43 listed Commonwealth countries (least developed and middle-income countries, including fragile and conflict-affected states) who could not otherwise afford UK study. Universities bid for places on specific approved courses and pay the living-cost part; the CSC pays tuition fees and airfare and approves the candidates the universities choose.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality and residence: you must be a citizen of an eligible Commonwealth country, or have refugee status granted by one, and be permanently resident in an eligible country. The 43 eligible countries are Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Saint Helena, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and The Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, The Gambia, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia.

Academic: you must be available to start UK study by September 2027. By September 2027 you must hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master's). Applicants who are still studying can apply, giving a projected completion date and transcripts to date; the first degree must be finished by the September of the start year.

High-income countries: you must not have studied or worked for one academic year or more in a high-income country. Distance learning from home at a university in a high-income country is allowed but must be declared.

Financial: you must be unable to afford UK study without the scholarship.

Documents: you must provide all required documents in the required format. Missing transcripts or missing pages make an application ineligible.

Not eligible: current or former UK government employees and their relatives; staff of the Association of Commonwealth Universities or the British Council; CSC Commissioners (current or former) and their relatives. Former employees of these bodies may apply three years after leaving. Anyone convicted of bribery may be banned from reapplying for up to five years.

Other rules: study must be full-time on an approved course at a participating university; the CSC does not require an IELTS or other English test, but universities may set their own English requirements. Only one scholarship offer can be accepted, although you may apply to several courses and universities. A scholarship cannot be combined with another award covering the same costs. Scholars sign an undertaking to return home before the student visa expires.
age_experience_notes: There is no age limit, but applicants should check any leave restrictions set by their employer. Work experience is not required (general FAQ).
funding_summary: Normally 12 months of study for one Master's degree. The CSC and the university share the cost: tuition fees are covered in full by agreement between the two, the CSC pays approved return airfare, and the university pays the monthly stipend (GBP 1,712, or GBP 2,000 at London-area universities), a thesis grant where applicable, and a study travel grant funded by the CSC. There is also a contribution to a mandatory TB test. The child allowance for single, widowed or divorced parents is only a partial contribution.
programmes_note: Only approved Master's courses at participating universities are eligible. The CSC lists each approved course under one of six development themes (Access, inclusion and opportunity; Improving population health, health systems and capacity; Promoting innovation and entrepreneurship; Science and technology for development; Strengthening peace, security and governance; Strengthening resilience and response to crises). The first 25 courses in the CSC list are shown here; the full list is on the CSC approved-courses page. Some course names in the application system differ from the names on the list (five courses are flagged). Not available for undergraduate or PhD study.
institutions_note: 47 UK universities take part, each with between 1 and 7 scholarships: Aberystwyth University, Bangor University, Bournemouth University, Brunel University London, Buckinghamshire New University, Cranfield University, Durham University, Imperial College London, King's College London, Liverpool Hope University, Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, London School of Economics and Political Science, London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Newcastle University, Queen's University Belfast, Royal Veterinary College, Sheffield Hallam University, SOAS University of London, St Mary's University, UCL, University of Aberdeen, Bath, Birmingham, Bristol, Cambridge, Chester, East Anglia, Edinburgh, Exeter, Glasgow, Hertfordshire, Hull, Leeds, Liverpool, Nottingham, Oxford, Portsmouth, Reading, Southampton, St Andrews, Stirling, Strathclyde, Surrey, Sussex, the West of England, Warwick and Wolverhampton. You choose a course, apply to that university for admission, and apply to the CSC; the university runs its own recruitment and nominates candidates. University notes on the CSC page: Bangor gives preference to residents of Uganda and Kenya who work with The Windle Trust; Bournemouth would prefer not to recruit CSC applicants from Ghana, India, Nigeria or Pakistan for MSc Public Health only; Oxford gives preference to underrepresented African countries for the MSt in Diplomatic Studies.

summary.detail: Full-time Master's study, normally 12 months, on an approved course at a participating UK university. One degree only; no concurrent courses. Taught in English at UK universities; the CSC sets no English test but universities may. Admission to the course is applied for separately from the scholarship.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition fees covered in full by agreement between the CSC and the university
benefits.conditions: Scholars pay nothing towards tuition. One degree only, full-time.

benefits.limit_text: GBP 1,712 per month, or GBP 2,000 per month at universities in the London metropolitan area (current rates)
benefits.conditions: Paid by the university. Normally for 12 months.

benefits.limit_text: Approved return airfare to and from the UK, paid by the CSC
benefits.conditions: Not covered: dependants' fares and journeys made before the award is confirmed. The general FAQ says scholars must leave the UK within one month of the end of the award or programme, whichever is earlier, or may lose airfare and excess baggage entitlements.

benefits.limit_text: Study travel grant for study-related travel within the UK or overseas
benefits.conditions: Paid by the university, funded by the CSC.
Where applicable; paid by the university, funded by the CSC.

benefits.conditions: Children must live at the same UK address. Only a partial contribution; scholars must be able to support accompanying family.

benefits.conditions: Under the CSC disability support statement.

requirements.text: A valid passport or national ID card showing photo, date of birth and country of citizenship (refugee status is also accepted as proof). Uploaded to the CSC online system by the deadline.

Full transcripts for all higher education qualifications, including to-date transcripts for current courses, with certified translations if not in English. Missing transcripts or missing pages make the application ineligible. You must obtain and upload your own transcripts; the CSC does not contact universities.

At least two references, signed, in PDF, on institutional letterhead or from an email showing the sender's details, in the referee's own words. Referees should say how long and in what capacity they know you, your suitability for the scholarship, your analytical ability, original thought and perseverance, your strengths and weaknesses and your development potential. The application form itself asks for three referees, one a current employer if applicable.

Application form content: all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications; up to 10 publications and prizes; employment history and how it relates to the UK programme; award objectives and how the scholarship will meet them; career plans for the five years after the scholarship and long-term; personal statement on how your background motivates impact at home, including barriers overcome; voluntary activities and leadership.
A detailed plan of study entered in the form, explaining why you chose the course and the university. You must write it yourself, and listing course options alone is not enough.

Admission to the chosen Master's course at a participating university, applied for separately under that university's own deadlines and rules. An offer letter is not required at the time of applying to the CSC.
Health and Disability Form, submitted before the Confirmation of Award is issued.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for candidates who are selected.

requirements.text: Eligibility checklist: the CSC recommends completing the Shared Scholarships eligibility checklist before submitting. Due-diligence checks need your agreement to the use of personal data; refusing means the CSC cannot proceed.

application_steps.title: Choose an approved course and apply for admission
application_steps.detail: Pick an approved Master's course at a participating UK university. You may apply to several courses and universities but may accept only one scholarship offer. Apply to the university and secure admission separately; check that university's deadlines and rules, which can differ from the CSC closing date.

application_steps.title: Register on the CSC online system and prepare answers
application_steps.detail: Register on the CSC online application system; two-factor authentication (smartphone or second email account) is needed at every login. Use the CSC template form and guidance to prepare answers offline, then enter them. Save often and do not refresh the browser, as unsaved data is lost. Complete the eligibility checklist first.

application_steps.title: Upload references and documents, then submit by the deadline
application_steps.detail: Collect references and upload passport or ID, transcripts and references as PDFs. Applications cannot be edited after submission. The CSC accepts nothing sent by email or post. There is no application fee. The closing date for 2027/28 is 16:00 GMT on Tuesday 8 December 2026.

application_steps.title: University selects and nominates candidates
application_steps.detail: Each participating university runs its own recruitment, chooses its candidates and nominates them to the CSC; nominations are due in March 2027. The CSC checks eligibility, and due-diligence checks are done before any formal agreement.

application_steps.title: Assessment criteria and provisional selection
application_steps.detail: The CSC criteria are candidate merit, quality of the study plan and potential development impact on the home country; the CSC prefers research-for-development potential and UK-Commonwealth partnerships, and all else being equal chooses candidates from disadvantaged or marginalised backgrounds. The university issues a provisional selection, subject to CSC approval and admission terms. Applicants are told by email, at times that vary by scholarship.

application_steps.title: Confirmation of Award, health form and visa
application_steps.detail: The CSC issues a Confirmation of Award after admission terms are agreed. A Health and Disability Form is needed before that letter. Start on the date in the Confirmation of Award and meet UK student visa rules set by UK Visas and Immigration. Sign an undertaking to return home before the student visa expires.

application_steps.title: Conditions while studying and leaving afterwards
application_steps.detail: Study full-time and live in the UK; get CSC approval before overseas travel and before any paid work. Changes to the plan of study need CSC agreement. Follow the CSC Code of Conduct. The award can be ended for unsatisfactory conduct, progress or attendance, or if the university suspends or ends registration. Extension of UK stay is considered only for moving from a Master's to a PhD under strict conditions, and the CSC gives no letters of support for post-award work or postdoctoral study.
